sources.name: UK general election 2024: results by constituency
sources.publisher: House of Commons Library / UK Parliament
sources.note: Every candidate's votes in all 650 seats. We group them by party (Workers Party and small parties go into 'Other parties').

sources.name: How Britain voted in the 2024 general election
sources.note: 42,119 adults polled 5–8 July 2024. Gives the vote share of each party by age, sex, social grade and education, and how big each group was among voters.

sources.name: How Britain voted in the 2024 election
sources.note: 17,394 adults, 5–8 July 2024. Our source for how White, Asian, Black and Mixed voters split (Ipsos warns the minority sub-group samples are small), plus turnout estimates for the fun facts, e.g. only 37% of 18–24s.

sources.name: Ethnic group, England and Wales: Census 2021
sources.note: Population by ethnic group (White 81.7%, Asian 9.3%, Black 4.0%, Mixed 2.9%, Other 2.1%). Combined with Ipsos turnout to size each group among voters.

sources.name: EU referendum results
sources.note: Remain 48.1%, Leave 51.9%. Used as a rough guide to how many 2024 voters were Remainers vs Leavers (people who didn't vote in 2016 are folded in).

sources.name: Half of us: turnout patterns at the 2024 general election
sources.note: Background on who didn't vote: just 52.8% of the voting-age population turned out.

sources.name: UK general election results 2010–2019
sources.publisher: House of Commons Library / UK Parliament
sources.note: Every candidate's votes in every seat at the 2010, 2015, 2017 and 2019 general elections.

sources.name: How Britain voted in 2010
sources.note: 10,211 adults over the campaign. Con/Lab/LD/Other shares and turnout by sex, age, class, housing and ethnicity, plus group sizes.

sources.name: How Britain voted in 2015
sources.note: 9,149 adults. Con/Lab/LD/UKIP/Green shares and turnout by sex, age, class, housing and ethnicity. Group sizes estimated from Ipsos's 2010 profile.

sources.name: How Britain voted in the 2017 election
sources.note: 7,505 adults. We use it for housing and ethnicity (Con/Lab/LD/UKIP/Other) and turnout.

sources.name: How Britain voted in the 2019 election
sources.note: 27,951 adults. We use it for housing and ethnicity (Con/Lab/LD/Other) and turnout.

sources.name: How Britain voted at the 2017 general election
sources.note: 52,615 adults. Full party shares and turnout by age, sex, social grade, education, work and the newspaper people read.

sources.name: How Britain voted in the 2019 general election
sources.note: 41,995 adults. Full party shares by age, sex, social grade, education, work, income and Brexit vote. No turnout, so group sizes use YouGov's 2017 turnout.

sources.name: Ethnicity and national identity in England and Wales: 2011
sources.note: 86% of people identified as White in 2011. Used with Ipsos turnout to size ethnic groups among voters, 2010–2019.
